tells.1: The comprehensive, evenly structured checklist feels templated, especially where confident business claims precede the unfinished financial analysis.
tells.2: Repeated 'Mitigation:' labels and 'Finance to complete' constructions give the memo a mechanically standardized voice.
tells.3: Repeated recommendation language and abstract phrases such as 'the most effective way possible' resemble AI padding, though neither establishes AI authorship.
tells.4: Bold lead-ins on nearly every bullet, uniform risk-treatment formulas, and generic labels such as 'Flexibility' make the presentation feel heavily templated.

reason: Version 1 best combines executive clarity with natural, direct sentences; version 3 sounds more individual but is repetitive and less precise. I would send version 1 after validating its unsupported claims and completing the financial figures and deadlines.
